answer.rationale: Competitive price pressure on SMB is immediate, but memory_73 and exp_73 show that matching discounts on price-sensitive SMB creates cohorts with -12% 30-day retention and poor renewal outcomes. This directly conflicts with the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Instead, referral_incentive addresses the underlying competitive threat by monetizing existing customer relationships and loyalty (memory_57 confirms referral works well in established customers without retention harm). This is defensible against churn because it rewards your existing base rather than racing to the bottom on pricing. Simultaneously, we should layer activation_messaging (memory_91) to re-engage at-risk SMB accounts with value realization rather than price alone. A standard_experiment on referral incentive targeting accounts in churn conversations can be validated quickly and scaled if it stems defection without the renewal-cohort damage of promotional pricing. This preserves the option to escalate to enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) for higher-ACV accounts showing competitive pressure.
